question: What are the two main parts that make up a basic computer system?
explanation: A computer system requires physical equipment to touch, known as hardware, and instructions to run it, known as software. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h1)

question: Why must a nurse understand basic computer systems used in clinical practice?

options.B: To maintain smooth patient care workflows
options.C: To write new hospital software programs
options.D: To fix major internal motherboard faults

explanation: Basic computer literacy helps nurses use digital tools efficiently and handle minor issues without stopping patient care. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h1)

question: Which device is used at the bedside to scan patient wristbands?
explanation: Barcode scanners read optical codes on patient bands to ensure accurate medication administration. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h2)

question: A nurse needs to show a doctor a laboratory result on a screen. Which device category is being used?
explanation: A monitor displays processed data visually, making it an output device. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h2)

question: What is the primary function of the CPU in a computer system?

options.A: Connecting the computer to the internet
options.D: Acting as the brain to process instructions

explanation: The CPU is responsible for executing program instructions and handling data processing tasks. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h3)

question: What happens to data stored in RAM when the computer loses power?

options.B: The data is sent to the printer
options.C: The data moves to the CPU

explanation: RAM is volatile memory, meaning it requires electrical power to retain its contents. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of a storage device in a healthcare computer system?

options.C: Retaining patient records over a long period
options.D: Entering text data through a physical keyboard

explanation: Storage devices keep data safe and accessible even after a computer is powered down. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h4)

question: How do storage devices differ from RAM?

options.A: Storage requires electrical power to keep files, unlike RAM
options.B: RAM is used to store thousands of past patient discharge files
options.C: Storage components process mathematical calculations for the CPU
options.D: Storage keeps data long-term, while RAM holds active data temporarily

explanation: RAM is fast, temporary workspace, whereas storage provides non-volatile retention of files. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h4)

question: Which of the following is an example of an operating system?
explanation: An operating system manages computer hardware and provides a platform for running other programs. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h5)

question: What is the main role of clinical application software in a hospital?

options.A: Managing the basic electrical startup of the computer
options.B: Providing specialized tools for charting and patient care
options.C: Physical storage of backup hard drives and cables
options.D: Translating typed text into barcode labels

explanation: Clinical applications are specific programs designed to assist healthcare workers with documentation and workflow tasks. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h5)

question: What type of network connects computers within a single hospital building?
explanation: A LAN connects computers and devices within a limited geographical area like a single clinic or hospital. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h6)

question: Why is network connectivity crucial for modern Electronic Health Record systems?

options.A: It automatically prints paper copies of every prescription written
options.B: It replaces the need for an operating system on ward computers
options.C: It allows instant sharing of patient data across different departments
options.D: It stops the computer hardware from overheating during heavy use

explanation: Networks enable multiple users in various locations to access and update the same patient records in real time. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h6)

question: What action should a nurse take before walking away from a workstation displaying patient data?

options.A: Lock or log out of the computer session
options.B: Turn off the physical monitor screen switch
options.C: Cover the keyboard with a protective cloth
options.D: Unplug the network cable from the wall

explanation: Locking the screen prevents unauthorized individuals from viewing confidential patient information. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h7)

question: Which behavior represents a breach of patient data privacy in a digital hospital environment?

options.A: Sharing lab results with the primary doctor treating the patient
options.B: Using a barcode scanner to verify a medication before giving it
options.C: Looking up the medical record of a neighbor who is not under your care
options.D: Logging into the electronic health record using your own secure password

explanation: Accessing patient files without a direct clinical need violates professional confidentiality and privacy laws. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h7)
